newsitem.title: UK: Cable & Wireless up amid switching out of BT.
newsitem.headline: Cable & Wireless up amid switching out of BT.

text.p: Cable & Wireless Plc shares hit a record on Thursday on switching from British Telecommunications Plc and continued support for shares in the company's Hongkong Telecommunications unit, analysts said.
The stock was up 15p at 609-1/2 by 1106 GMT, after earlier setting a record 612p, in moderate volume of 3.7 million shares.
Analysts noted that C&W shares had enjoyed a strong run since early June, when HK Telecom said its parent was in talks on future co-operation with China.

That announcement was followed by China Telecom buying a 5.5 percent stake from C&W and analysts expect China to continue increasing its stake. China Telecom said overnight it foresees increased co-operation with HK Telecom.
Analyst Steve Scruton at Credit Lyonnais Laing said HK Telecom shares had risen by a third since the China deal and C&W had lagged that advance.

"C&W's discount to its sum-of-parts has been increasing," Scruton said. "At the same time (C&W chief executive) Dick Brown has been delivering on his promises, which is more than you can say for some companies...and if you're selling BT, where else in the sector do you put your money?"
BT was down 14-1/2p at 431 amid concern about its planned alliance with MCI.
Analyst Andrew Harrington at Salomon Brothers said he remained positive on C&W shares.

"UK institutions have been underweight in C&W for quite a long time and they are topping up their holdings," Harrington said. "The Hong Kong market has been very strong and I strongly believe there will be a merger at some time."
